text: I was easily distracted by little things.
I found it difficult to resume a task after being interrupted.
I avoided or disliked tasks that needed sustained mental effort (e.g., completing forms or reading lengthy documents).
I had trouble changing how I was doing something, even when it wasn't working.
I had trouble staying awake during the day even after getting enough sleep the night before.
I found it hard to remember things.
I needed help from others to take care of myself or my home (e.g., I found it difficult to shop, clean, or cook independently).
I found it difficult to recall recent events.
It got harder for me to do familiar things (e.g., using tools or driving a car).
I had a hard time finding my way around even in familiar environments.
I couldn't use the living areas of my home because they were cluttered with my things.
I found it hard to part with my possessions, regardless of their actual value.
I lost things that I needed for tasks or activities (e.g., phone, wallet, keys, glasses, documents).
I found it difficult to understand and use facial expressions, gestures, tone of voice, eye contact, or body language.
I found it hard to adjust my behaviour to suit different social contexts.
I had difficulty understanding what others were trying to say.
I was unable to have normal back-and-forth conversations (e.g., I did not give other people a turn to speak or provide enough background information for others to follow).
I did not respond when someone tried to interact with me.
I talked too much (e.g., talked at inappropriate times, interrupted or talked over other people, or took over conversations).
I spoke quickly without stopping, changing topics a lot.
I felt "on the go" and was unable to sit still for any length of time (e.g., in a meeting or when having dinner at a restaurant).
I fidgeted a lot.
I felt internal pressure to keep talking.
I only talked about one topic even when others were not interested or said they wanted to talk about something else.
I had intense interests in specific objects or topics.
I was very sensitive to specific sights, sounds, smells, tastes or textures.
I insisted that things had to be done in exactly the same way (e.g., I was very distressed by small changes).
I insisted on perfection in everything I did.
I felt like I was short of breath.
It felt like my heart was fluttering or skipping beats.
I had muscle tension (e.g., aches and pains or tightness in my shoulders, back, neck, or jaws).
I experienced substantial pain in one or more areas of my body.
I had a feeling of heat spreading through me (e.g., in my head and neck).
I ate large amounts of food when I didn't feel hungry.
I felt disgusted, depressed, or very guilty about eating a lot in a short period of time.
My body weight or shape had a lot of influence on how I felt about myself.
I feared gaining weight.
I fasted (i.e., avoided eating) to control my weight.
I was more extroverted than usual (i.e., sociable, talkative, and excitable).
I had a strong feeling of well-being or were overly happy (i.e., "felt euphoric" or "on top of the world").
I was unrestrained in expressing my feelings (e.g., overly enthusiastic or overly friendly).
I kept my emotions to myself.
I preferred to keep romance out of my life.
I was not interested in having sexual relationships.
